edit.description: the two relocated-root arms that return green over a leg nothing judged, and the comments that argue the verdict already says so
the two arms' cases, which no case in the file reaches today

summary: the new-blocker and goal-rank gates spell their relocated-root arm on the field the engine persists, so a leg nothing judged stops reading as a judged pass

per.section: A green verdict is proven non-vacuous

acceptance: under a relocated state root the new-blocker gate reports its verdict as skipped, having judged no edge there, and the goal-rank gate states on its verdict that it ruled on placement alone — so a reader of the tick verdict tells either from a judged pass without parsing the message's English, and both arms gain the cases nothing reaches today
tests: a new-blocker verdict under a relocated state root is reported skipped, not as a judged green
a goal-rank verdict under a relocated state root states that it ruled on placement alone

interface.changes: a tick verdict's new-blocker gate row carries `skipped` under a relocated state root, and the goal-rank row carries a `verdict` discriminant there, both copied verbatim by the dispatcher
interface.hides: that a gate which judged nothing, and one which judged half of what it names, reported the same green as one that judged everything
interface.rejected: spelling `skipped` on the goal-rank arm too — placement is judged there, so the field would claim nothing ran, where `verdict` is the engine's declared discriminant for why a gate ruled as it did

notes: Measured on this tip: `:618`-`:622` returns `ok: true` with no `skipped` having judged no edge at all, `:463`-`:467` the same having judged placement alone; both comments claim the verdict says so, which only the message does. `GateResult.skipped` (`src/Gate.ts`) rules the first — a green without it claims it ran. The sibling records and slice-state arms, and both empty-queue arms, spell theirs. No case reaches either arm.
